published_prior_art.cite: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE: Theorem 1 gives the faster bounded-density lower benchmark, not a band-only density-coupled slowdown.
Kennedy2023DRCATE: Corollary 3 gives the same upper-rate branch under high-level nuisance and Gram conditions, but not its derivation uniformly from the primitive fixed density band.
KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE plus Kennedy2023DRCATE: neither supplies a matched lower and feasible upper bound over one fixed two-sided band-only CATE class.
KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE: supplies the comparator rate; the strict open-region separation is an algebraic consequence of the proposed new lower bound.
Kennedy2023DRCATE: the lp-R-learner analysis contains the oracle local-regression branch under known nuisances.
Kennedy2023DRCATE and LiuLiGuLiu2026StabilizedHOIF leave the relevant non-oracle/minimax and beyond-rank questions unresolved in their respective settings.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 797-798, Section 3, Theorem 1 and Remark 2; Appendix B.8
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 gives the pointwise CATE lower rate for a model with covariate density bounded above; Remark 2 says that attaining it needs further density conditions, and Appendix B.8 describes the matching density-qualified class.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 5, Theorem 3 and Corollary 3; Section 6 discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The lp-R-learner upper analysis assumes bounded density, fitted-propensity truncation, sample-Gram control, and local nuisance conditions; Corollary 3 uses k asymptotic to n/log^2 n and yields the n^{-2s/d}=n^{-(alpha+beta)/d} non-oracle branch up to logs.

The empirical HOIF construction removes a multivariate density-smoothness requirement for global missing-data/ATE-type functionals by estimating the Gram object from data; it is not a pointwise CATE minimax theorem.

The paper studies stabilized same-sample higher-order estimators for global bilinear forms and contrasts them with empirical-HOIF constructions restricted below sample rank; it does not state the proposed localized band-only CATE frontier.
The article concerns minimax estimation of a variance function in heteroscedastic nonparametric regression with random design, using a distinct regression-functional target.
The paper proves asymptotic normality for changing-kernel quadratic U-statistics, including slower-than-root-n regimes; it does not establish a pointwise CATE minimax rate.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a short corollary that explicitly identifies the KBRW lower-bound construction's density support condition and proves that the fixed two-sided band class is neither its attainment class nor a mere reparametrization of it.

State the uniform Gram-conditioning lemma for the chosen partition series as an intermediate target, with its dependence on k_n, f_- and f_+, to make the primitive-to-feasible upper-bound bridge independently reusable.

Extend the density-coupled lower construction to a second nontrivial ordering beyond beta<alpha, or give a sharp boundary result at alpha=beta, to reduce reliance on one asymmetric low-smoothness wedge.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the density-coupled lower bound and primitive Gram-conditioning proof as the two load-bearing derivation targets.
